## ducta start

Start data pipelines directly without orchestration

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--env`, `-e` | Execution environment (base, dev, sandbox, prod, or sandbox_<developer>). Defaults to 'base' when omitted. — default `base` |
| `--pipeline`, `-p` | Pipeline name to execute |
| `--node`, `-n` | Specific node to execute (optional) |
| `--mode`, `-m` | Execution mode for streaming/hybrid pipelines. Either way the command runs while the queries do (they live in its process): 'async' (default) reports their status and stops them on Ctrl+C; 'sync' waits inside the engine — one of `sync`, `async`; default `async` |
| `--start-date` | Start date (YYYY-MM-DD) |
| `--end-date` | End date (YYYY-MM-DD) |
| `--base-path` | Project directory (default: the current directory or its nearest parent holding ducta.yaml) |
| `--log-level` | Logging level — one of `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARNING`, `ERROR`, `CRITICAL`; default `INFO` |
| `--log-file` | Custom log file path |
| `--verbose` | Enable verbose output (DEBUG) |
| `--quiet` | Reduce output (ERROR only) |
| `--model-version` | Model version for ML pipelines |
| `--hyperparams` | Hyperparameters as JSON string |
| `--sweep` | Hyperparameter sweep spec (YAML/JSON file). List values are expanded into the cartesian product and one run is executed per combination, all tagged with a common sweep_id in the experiment tracker |
| `--search` | Drive a real search strategy from the pipeline's hyperparams_config (algorithm: grid\|random\|bayesian, honoring n_trials and objective.metric) instead of the flat cartesian product --sweep expands. Each trial's objective value is fed back to the strategy, so Bayesian search learns between trials |
| `--search-metric` | Objective metric to optimize, overriding hyperparams_config.objective.metric. Point it at a validation metric: selecting on a test metric invalidates it |
| `--search-trials` | Trial budget for --search (random/bayesian), overriding n_trials |
| `--no-sweep-reuse` | Recompute every node on each sweep/search trial. By default the trial-invariant upstream nodes are materialized once and reused, since trials differ only in hyperparameters |
| `--sweep-parallel` | Run N sweep/search trials concurrently, each in its own process and its own output directory. Mutually exclusive with upstream reuse (an isolated trial has nothing shared to reuse), and not applied to Bayesian search, which needs each trial's result before choosing the next. Use it when training dominates the runtime, and --no-sweep-reuse off (the default) when feature engineering does — default `1` |
| `--max-sweep-size` | Cap on the number of combinations a --sweep/--search grid may expand to (default: 50). Mirrors the API's max_sweep_size setting for the CLI path |
| `--validate-only` | Validate configuration without executing the pipeline |
| `--dry-run` | Log actions without executing the pipeline |
| `--sanity-only` | Run sanity checks on all node inputs without executing the pipeline |
| `--reuse-upstream` | In a depends_on chain, skip upstream pipelines whose outputs are already materialized (reads them from disk instead of recomputing) |
| `--rerun-all` | Force the full depends_on chain to re-run, ignoring any chain-reuse configuration |

## ducta stream

Manage real-time streaming pipelines

### ducta stream run

Run streaming pipeline

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--config`, `-c` | ducta.yaml, or any file or directory inside the project (default: the project containing the current directory) |
| `--pipeline`, `-p` | Pipeline name to execute — *(required)* |
| `--env`, `-e` | Execution environment (base, dev, prod, …) — default `base` |
| `--mode`, `-m` | Either way the command runs while the queries do (they live in its process): 'async' (default) reports their status and stops them on Ctrl+C; 'sync' waits inside the engine — one of `sync`, `async`; default `async` |
| `--model-version` | Model version for ML pipelines |
| `--hyperparams` | Hyperparameters as JSON string |
| `--transforms-module` | Python module path(s) to import before starting the pipeline. Each module must expose a register_transforms(registry) function. Example: src.streaming_fraud_realtime |

### ducta stream status

Check streaming pipeline status

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--config`, `-c` | ducta.yaml, or any file or directory inside the project (default: the project containing the current directory) |
| `--env`, `-e` | Execution environment — default `base` |
| `--execution-id`, `-i` | Specific execution ID to check |
| `--output-format`, `--format`, `-f` | Output format — one of `table`, `json`; default `table` |

### ducta stream stop

Stop streaming pipeline

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--config`, `-c` | ducta.yaml, or any file or directory inside the project (default: the project containing the current directory) |
| `--env`, `-e` | Execution environment — default `base` |
| `--execution-id`, `-i` | Execution ID to stop — *(required)* |
| `--timeout`, `-t` | Timeout in seconds — default `60` |

## ducta template

Generate Ducta project templates and boilerplate code

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--template` | Template type to generate |
| `--project-name` | Project name for template |
| `--output-path` | Output path for generated files |
| `--sandbox-developers` | List of developer names for sandbox environments |
| `--format` | Format of ducta, catalog and pipeline files (default: yaml, which keeps the explanatory comments; toml and json are the same project without them) — one of `yaml`, `toml`, `json`; default `yaml` |
| `--no-sample-code` | Do not include sample code in generated template |
| `--list-templates` | List available templates |
| `--evidence-level` | How much evidence each run must leave (written to global_config): off = no certificate; record = certificate, a write failure only warns (default); required = a run without its certificate fails; signed = required + HMAC signature, preflight fails without DUCTA_CERTIFICATE_KEY — one of `off`, `record`, `required`, `signed`; default `record` |

## ducta config

Manage Ducta configuration and discovery

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--base-path` | Project directory (default: the current directory or its nearest parent holding ducta.yaml) |

### ducta config list-pipelines

List available pipelines

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--env` | Environment to use for listing |
| `--filter` | Filter pipelines by name (case-insensitive substring match) |
| `--output-format`, `--format` | Output format: table (default), json, or list — one of `table`, `json`, `list`; default `table` |

### ducta config pipeline-info

Show pipeline information

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--pipeline` | Pipeline name — *(required)* |
| `--env` | Environment to use |

### ducta config validate

Import node functions, check signatures, and resolve I/O keys without running Spark. Reports every configuration error up front.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--pipeline` | Pipeline to validate (default: all pipelines) |
| `--env` | Environment to use |
| `--output-format` | json: one JSON document on stdout — every problem with its file, line, node and suggested fix — for CI and AI assistants — one of `rich`, `json`; default `rich` |

### ducta config show

The project after templates (extends), defaults and the environment's overrides are applied: what Ducta actually runs. Use --format to read it as YAML, TOML or JSON.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--env` | Environment to resolve (default: the base project) |
| `--pipeline` | Only this pipeline and the datasets it touches |
| `--format` | Output format (default: yaml) — one of `yaml`, `toml`, `json`; default `yaml` |
| `--engine` | Print the five documents the engine reads instead of the project's shape |
| `--ml` | What each ML node will be given: its split and where it was declared, whether it must apply it, its merged hyperparameters and model version |

### ducta config explain

Follows a value through the file, the pipeline template, defaults and the environment's overrides, with the file and line of each step.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `<path>` | e.g. settings.max_parallel_nodes or pipelines.etl.nodes.load.retry — *(required)* |
| `--env` | Environment to resolve (default: base) |

### ducta config diff

Show what differs between two environments

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `<env_a>` | First environment (use 'base' for none) — *(required)* |
| `<env_b>` | Second environment — *(required)* |

### ducta config convert

Rewrites ducta, catalog, pipelines/ and templates/ as YAML, TOML or JSON in a new directory. Comments are not carried over; your Python and data are not copied.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--to` | one of `yaml`, `toml`, `json`; *(required)* |
| `--out` | New directory to write into — *(required)* |

### ducta config schema

Print (or write) the JSON Schema of the format-2 configuration files

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--out` | Directory to write project/catalog/pipeline.json into |

## ducta ui

Launch the Ducta React frontend and FastAPI backend

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--port` | Port to run the UI server on (default: 8000) — default `8000` |
| `--host` | Host to bind the UI server to (default: 127.0.0.1) — default `127.0.0.1` |
| `--no-browser` | Do not automatically open the browser |
| `--source` | Workspace source path or Git URL to load automatically |
| `--db` | Path for the SQLite execution history database (default: ~/.ducta/executions.db) |
| `--enable-terminal` | Enable the embedded web terminal (PTY). SECURITY: grants arbitrary shell execution to authenticated users. Off by default. |

### ducta server start

Start the local Ducta server with the MLflow-style web dashboard

| Option | What it does |

## ducta profile

Measure a dataset and emit a reviewable spec derived from what is actually in it, instead of requiring the thresholds to be known in advance. Runs standalone on a file: no project, no DAG, no Spark.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--input`, `-i` | Path to the data file — *(required)* |
| `--format`, `-f` | Input file format (default: parquet) — one of `parquet`, `csv`, `json`; default `parquet` |
| `--output`, `-o` | Write the proposed spec here (default: print it to stdout) |
| `--strictness` | How close the proposed bounds sit to what was observed (default: balanced) — one of `strict`, `balanced`, `lax`; default `balanced` |
| `--sample-rows` | Measure columns from a sample of at most N rows (row count stays exact) |
| `--dataset-name` | Name for the dataset in the spec (default: the file stem) |
| `--output-format` | How to render the profile (default: rich) — one of `rich`, `json`; default `rich` |

## ducta quality

Run, inspect, and validate Ducta data quality checks

### ducta quality list

List all registered quality checks (built-in and custom)

### ducta quality run

Run quality checks standalone on a data file

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--input`, `-i` | Path to input data file — *(required)* |
| `--format`, `-f` | Input file format (default: parquet) — one of `parquet`, `csv`, `json`; default `parquet` |
| `--config`, `-c` | Path to a TOML/YAML file with check config (checks table) — *(required)* |
| `--fail-fast` | Stop on first failing check |
| `--output-format` | Report output format (default: rich) — one of `rich`, `json`; default `rich` |

### ducta quality report

Show stored quality reports for a dataset

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--dataset`, `-d` | Dataset name whose reports to display — *(required)* |
| `--workspace`, `-w` | Workspace root path (default: current directory) — default `.` |
| `--run-id`, `-r` | Specific run ID to display (default: latest) |
| `--all` | List all stored run IDs for the dataset |
| `--output-format` | Report output format (default: rich) — one of `rich`, `json`; default `rich` |
| `--env`, `-e` | Environment to resolve the project's real quality.output storage from (base, dev, sandbox, prod, ...), instead of the standalone --workspace/.quality convention used by 'ducta quality run'. Reads reports a real pipeline run persisted. |
| `--pipeline`, `-p` | Pipeline name the report was recorded under (as named in config/pipelines, e.g. 'golden.transformation'). A report saved by a real pipeline run is scoped under its pipeline name, not the standalone default — omitting this when --env is a real project looks in the wrong place and reports no reports found. |
| `--base-path` | Project directory (default: the current directory or its nearest parent holding ducta.yaml) |

### ducta quality trend

Show score time-series for a dataset

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--dataset`, `-d` | Dataset name — *(required)* |
| `--workspace`, `-w` | Workspace root path (default: .) — default `.` |
| `--last`, `-n` | Number of recent scores to show (default: 20) — default `20` |
| `--output-format` | Output format (default: rich) — one of `rich`, `json`; default `rich` |
| `--env`, `-e` | Environment to resolve the project's real quality.output storage from, instead of the standalone --workspace convention. |
| `--pipeline`, `-p` | Pipeline name the score history was recorded under (see 'ducta quality report --help'). Omitting this when --env is a real project looks in the wrong place and reports no history. |
| `--base-path` | Project directory (default: the current directory or its nearest parent holding ducta.yaml) |

### ducta quality score

Show composite pipeline quality score for a run

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--run-id`, `-r` | Pipeline run ID — *(required)* |
| `--workspace`, `-w` | Workspace root path (default: .) — default `.` |
| `--output-format` | Output format (default: rich) — one of `rich`, `json`; default `rich` |
| `--env`, `-e` | Environment to resolve the project's real quality.output storage from, instead of the standalone --workspace convention. |
| `--base-path` | Project directory (default: the current directory or its nearest parent holding ducta.yaml) |

### ducta quality validate-config

Validate quality config for a node without executing

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--node`, `-n` | Node name whose quality config to validate — *(required)* |
| `--env`, `-e` | Environment whose configuration to check — default `base` |
| `--base-path` | Project directory (default: the current directory or its nearest parent holding ducta.yaml) |

## ducta experiment

List, inspect and compare MLOps experiment tracking data

### ducta experiment list

List recent experiments

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--storage-path` | MLOps storage path (Optional, auto-discovered by default) |
| `--env` | Project environment to resolve the storage path from (e.g. dev, prod) — auto-discovery requires this |
| `--pipeline` | Pipeline name (schema.pipeline) to resolve a per-pipeline storage path — matches how a real run resolves its own path when no global 'mlops_path' override is set. Omit to look at the environment's shared/default MLOps directory instead. |
| `--limit` | Maximum number of experiments to show (default: all) |

### ducta experiment runs

List the runs of one experiment

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `<experiment_id>` | Experiment id (see `experiment list`) — *(required)* |
| `--storage-path` | MLOps storage path (Optional, auto-discovered by default) |
| `--env` | Project environment to resolve the storage path from (e.g. dev, prod) — auto-discovery requires this |
| `--pipeline` | Pipeline name (schema.pipeline) to resolve a per-pipeline storage path — matches how a real run resolves its own path when no global 'mlops_path' override is set. |
| `--status` | Only runs in this status — one of `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `scheduled` |
| `--limit` | Maximum number of runs (newest first) |
| `--output-format` | Output format: a text table or JSON (default: rich) — one of `rich`, `json`; default `rich` |

### ducta experiment show

Show one run: parameters, metrics, artifacts

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `<run_id>` | Run id, or a unique prefix of it — *(required)* |
| `--storage-path` | MLOps storage path (Optional, auto-discovered by default) |
| `--env` | Project environment to resolve the storage path from (e.g. dev, prod) — auto-discovery requires this |
| `--pipeline` | Pipeline name (schema.pipeline) to resolve a per-pipeline storage path — matches how a real run resolves its own path when no global 'mlops_path' override is set. |
| `--output-format` | Output format: text or JSON (default: rich) — one of `rich`, `json`; default `rich` |

### ducta experiment compare

Compare the parameters and metrics of runs

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `<run_ids>` | Two or more run ids (or unique prefixes) — *(required)* |
| `--storage-path` | MLOps storage path (Optional, auto-discovered by default) |
| `--env` | Project environment to resolve the storage path from (e.g. dev, prod) — auto-discovery requires this |
| `--pipeline` | Pipeline name (schema.pipeline) to resolve a per-pipeline storage path — matches how a real run resolves its own path when no global 'mlops_path' override is set. |
| `--output-format` | Output format: a text table or JSON (default: rich) — one of `rich`, `json`; default `rich` |

## ducta model

Promote, garbage collect, and manage registered models

### ducta model promote

Promote a model version to a new stage

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `<name>` | Model name — *(required)* |
| `<version>` | Model version: the whole number the registry assigned (3 or v3) — *(required)* |
| `<stage>` | Target stage — one of `staging`, `production`, `archived`; *(required)* |
| `--storage-path` | MLOps storage path (Optional, auto-discovered by default) |
| `--env` | Project environment to resolve the storage path from (e.g. dev, prod) — auto-discovery requires this |
| `--pipeline` | Pipeline name (schema.pipeline) to resolve a per-pipeline storage path — matches how a real run resolves its own path when no global 'mlops_path' override is set. |
| `--force` | Bypass the promotion policy gate (the bypass is audit-logged) |

### ducta model gc

Garbage collect old model versions

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | Show what would be deleted without deleting |
| `--storage-path` | MLOps storage path (Optional, auto-discovered by default) |
| `--env` | Project environment to resolve the storage path from (e.g. dev, prod) — auto-discovery requires this |
| `--pipeline` | Pipeline name (schema.pipeline) to resolve a per-pipeline storage path — matches how a real run resolves its own path when no global 'mlops_path' override is set. Omit to garbage-collect the environment's shared/default MLOps directory instead. |

## ducta init

Initialize Ducta pipeline components (ingestion, etc.)

### ducta init project

Create a new Ducta project: ducta.<ext>, catalog/<layer>.<ext>, quality/profiles.<ext>, pipelines/<layer>.<domain>.<ext>, the Python the nodes run, and the editor schemas. `ducta template` writes the same projects with every dataset in one catalog file (--layout single here).

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--name` | Project name — *(required)* |
| `--type` | What the project does (default: batch, a bronze/silver/gold ETL) — one of `batch`, `ml`, `streaming`, `hybrid`; default `batch` |
| `--format` | Format of the configuration files (default: yaml, which keeps the comments) — one of `yaml`, `toml`, `json`; default `yaml` |
| `--path` | Directory to create (default: ./<name>; it must be empty or new) |
| `--layout` | split: catalog/ by layer + quality/profiles (default); single: one catalog file — one of `split`, `single`; default `split` |

### ducta init ingestion

Simple database connection management for Ducta ingestion

#### ducta init ingestion setup

Interactive wizard to configure a new database connection

#### ducta init ingestion list

List all configured database connections

#### ducta init ingestion test

Test a database connection

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--source` | Connection name to test — *(required)* |

#### ducta init ingestion info

Show connection details

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--source` | Connection name to show — *(required)* |

## ducta certify

Every terminating run writes a tamper-evident Run Certificate (${output_path}/${environment}/.ducta/runs/<run_id>/certificate.json by default). List, show, or verify them.

### ducta certify list

List run certificates

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--dir` | Runs directory (default: resolved per environment from config) |
| `--env` | Environment to scope the search to (default: search all environments) |

### ducta certify show

Show a certificate (human-readable by default)

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--run-id` | Run id (or a unique prefix) — *(required)* |
| `--dir` | Runs directory (default: resolved per environment from config) |
| `--env` | Environment to scope the search to (default: search all environments) |
| `--json` | Print the full certificate as raw JSON |

### ducta certify verify

Verify a certificate (tamper check, optionally re-run to prove reproducibility)

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--run-id` | Run id (or a unique prefix) — *(required)* |
| `--dir` | Runs directory (default: resolved per environment from config) |
| `--env` | Environment to scope the search to (default: search all environments) |
| `--reproduce` | Re-run the pipeline and confirm every output reproduces the certificate |
| `--start-date` | Start date for the reproduction run |
| `--end-date` | End date for the reproduction run |

### ducta certify diff

Compare two run certificates (config, outputs, quality)

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `<run_a>` | First run id (or a unique prefix) — *(required)* |
| `<run_b>` | Second run id (or a unique prefix) — *(required)* |
| `--dir` | Runs directory (default: resolved per environment from config) |
| `--env` | Environment to scope the search to (default: search all environments) |

## ducta ai

Choose a model (local: Ollama, LM Studio, any OpenAI-compatible server; remote: Anthropic, OpenAI) and draft pipelines with it. A draft is validated like an unsaved edit in the UI and written only when you accept it; nothing is run or committed. Settings live in ~/.ducta/ai.toml.

### ducta ai setup

Choose the provider and model

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--provider` | one of `ollama`, `lmstudio`, `openai`, `anthropic`, `openai_compatible`; *(required)* |
| `--model` | Model name (default: the largest code model a local server serves) |
| `--base-url` | Endpoint, e.g. http://localhost:8000/v1 |
| `--api-key-env` | Name of the variable holding the key (never the key itself) |
| `--effort` | Anthropic: reasoning effort — one of `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` |

### ducta ai login

Keep an API key in the system keychain

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--provider` | Default: the configured one — one of `ollama`, `lmstudio`, `openai`, `anthropic`, `openai_compatible` |

### ducta ai logout

Remove the API key from the keychain

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--provider` | Default: the configured one — one of `ollama`, `lmstudio`, `openai`, `anthropic`, `openai_compatible` |

### ducta ai doctor

Show the configuration and check the model answers

### ducta ai new

Draft a new pipeline from a description

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `<request>` | What to build, e.g. "silver pipeline that cleans orders" — *(required)* |
| `--base-path` | Project directory (default: the current directory or its nearest parent holding ducta.yaml) |
| `--attempts` | Times the model may fix validation problems (default 3) |
| `--write` | Write the draft once it validates |
| `--yes` | Do not ask before writing |
| `--force` | Write even if it does not validate |
| `--output-format` | Output format (json prints the draft) — one of `rich`, `json`; default `rich` |

### ducta ai fix

Draft a fix for a pipeline: its validation problems, a run's error, or a note

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `<pipeline>` | Pipeline to fix — *(required)* |
| `--note` | What is wrong, in your words (e.g. "amounts come in cents") |
| `--error-file` | File holding the error or traceback a run failed with |
| `--base-path` | Project directory (default: the current directory or its nearest parent holding ducta.yaml) |
| `--attempts` | Times the model may fix validation problems (default 3) |
| `--write` | Write the draft once it validates |
| `--yes` | Do not ask before writing |
| `--force` | Write even if it does not validate |
| `--output-format` | Output format (json prints the draft) — one of `rich`, `json`; default `rich` |

### ducta ai quality

Ducta measures the node's output in --env (column statistics only: the model never sees a row), the model proposes the node's `quality` block, and Ducta runs it on that data — a check that would fail goes back to the model.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `<pipeline>` | Pipeline holding the node — *(required)* |
| `<node>` | Node whose output to check — *(required)* |
| `--env` | Environment whose data is measured — default `dev` |
| `--note` | What matters to you (e.g. "order_id is the key") |
| `--base-path` | Project directory (default: the current directory or its nearest parent holding ducta.yaml) |
| `--attempts` | Times the model may fix what is found (default 3) |
| `--write` | Write the checks once it validates |
| `--yes` | Do not ask before writing |
| `--force` | Write even if it does not validate |
| `--output-format` | Output format (json prints the draft) — one of `rich`, `json`; default `rich` |

### ducta ai document

Adds a one-line description where there is none, and lists the columns that hold personal data (metadata.pii). Only what is missing is added; nothing else in the files changes.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--env` | Environment whose data gives columns — default `dev` |
| `--note` | Anything the model should know (e.g. "in Spanish") |
| `--base-path` | Project directory (default: the current directory or its nearest parent holding ducta.yaml) |
| `--attempts` | Times the model may fix what is found (default 3) |
| `--write` | Write the descriptions once it validates |
| `--yes` | Do not ask before writing |
| `--force` | Write even if it does not validate |
| `--output-format` | Output format (json prints the draft) — one of `rich`, `json`; default `rich` |

### ducta ai explain

Ducta diagnoses the error (the kind of failure, the line of your code it was raised on); the model explains it in plain words. Nothing is changed. In the web app, a failed run's page explains it from the run itself.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--error-file` | File holding the error or traceback (- for stdin) — *(required)* |
| `--note` | What you were doing, or what you already tried |
| `--base-path` | Project directory (default: the current directory or its nearest parent holding ducta.yaml) |
| `--output-format` | Output format (json for scripts) — one of `rich`, `json`; default `rich` |

### ducta ai review

Ducta checks the node first (a retried node that appends, runs near their timeout, I/O or collect() inside the function, credentials in the code…); the model adds what it sees in the code, the effective settings and the last runs. A finding of the model's that cites a line or setting that does not exist is dropped. Nothing is changed.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `<pipeline>` | Pipeline holding the node — *(required)* |
| `<node>` | Node to review — *(required)* |
| `--env` | Environment whose settings and runs to use — default `dev` |
| `--note` | What worries you (e.g. "it got slow last week") |
| `--no-ai` | Only Ducta's own checks: no model is asked |
| `--fail-on` | Exit 3 when a finding is this severe or more (for CI) — one of `high`, `medium`, `low` |
| `--base-path` | Project directory (default: the current directory or its nearest parent holding ducta.yaml) |
| `--output-format` | Output format (json for scripts) — one of `rich`, `json`; default `rich` |

### ducta ai revise

Ask for changes to a draft (a new draft)

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `<draft_id>` | Draft id (or a unique prefix) — *(required)* |
| `--note` | What to change (e.g. "group by day") — *(required)* |
| `--base-path` | Project directory (default: the current directory or its nearest parent holding ducta.yaml) |
| `--attempts` | Times the model may fix validation problems (default 3) |
| `--write` | Write the draft once it validates |
| `--yes` | Do not ask before writing |
| `--force` | Write even if it does not validate |
| `--output-format` | Output format (json prints the draft) — one of `rich`, `json`; default `rich` |

### ducta ai drafts

List the project's drafts

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--base-path` | Project directory (default: the current directory or its nearest parent holding ducta.yaml) |

### ducta ai apply

Write a saved draft to the project

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `<draft_id>` | Draft id (or a unique prefix), from `ducta ai new` — *(required)* |
| `--base-path` | Project directory (default: the current directory or its nearest parent holding ducta.yaml) |
| `--yes` | Do not ask before writing |
| `--force` | Write even if it does not validate |

### ducta ai architect

The model designs a blueprint (datasets, pipelines, contracts, logic in words); Ducta checks it without a model, writes the YAML itself and has the model write only the functions. `check` and `scaffold` need no model.

#### ducta ai architect plan

Design a blueprint for a request (a draft)

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `<request>` | What to build, e.g. "revenue per store and day" — *(required)* |
| `--note` | Answers to the model's questions, or what matters to you |
| `--attempts` | Times the model may fix what is found (default 3) |
| `--base-path` | Project directory (default: the current directory or its nearest parent holding ducta.yaml) |
| `--output-format` | Output format (json prints the draft) — one of `rich`, `json`; default `rich` |

#### ducta ai architect check

Check a blueprint file without a model

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `<blueprint>` | The blueprint's YAML file — *(required)* |
| `--base-path` | Project directory (default: the current directory or its nearest parent holding ducta.yaml) |
| `--output-format` | Output format (json for scripts and assistants) — one of `rich`, `json`; default `rich` |

#### ducta ai architect scaffold

Turn a blueprint file into a draft with stub functions, without a model

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `<blueprint>` | The blueprint's YAML file — *(required)* |
| `--write` | Write the draft once it validates |
| `--yes` | Do not ask before writing |
| `--base-path` | Project directory (default: the current directory or its nearest parent holding ducta.yaml) |
| `--output-format` | Output format (json prints the draft) — one of `rich`, `json`; default `rich` |

#### ducta ai architect build

Build a blueprint into one draft (the model writes the code)

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `<blueprint>` | A blueprint draft id (from `plan`) or a blueprint file — *(required)* |
| `--attempts` | Times the model may fix each module (default 3) |
| `--write` | Write the draft once it validates |
| `--yes` | Do not ask before writing |
| `--force` | Write even if it does not validate |
| `--base-path` | Project directory (default: the current directory or its nearest parent holding ducta.yaml) |
| `--output-format` | Output format (json prints the draft) — one of `rich`, `json`; default `rich` |

#### ducta ai architect verify

Validate built pipelines; run them in dev and snapshot their tests

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `<pipelines>` | Pipelines to verify (default: all) |
| `--env` | Where to run them (never a protected one) — default `dev` |
| `--run` | Run them, in dependency order |
| `--tests` | Write snapshot tests once they ran |
| `--start-date` | For pipelines that require dates (YYYY-MM-DD) |
| `--end-date` | For pipelines that require dates (YYYY-MM-DD) |
| `--base-path` | Project directory (default: the current directory or its nearest parent holding ducta.yaml) |
| `--output-format` | Output format (json for scripts) — one of `rich`, `json`; default `rich` |

### ducta ai sentinel

Rules decide: a failed run is diagnosed and a fixed table picks what to do. Re-runs happen only where sentinel: in ducta.yaml allows them, never in a protected environment; the rest is escalated, with an explanation and a fix draft from the model when one is configured. Only `watch` acts.

#### ducta ai sentinel status

Whether Sentinel watches this project, and where it may act

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--base-path` | Project directory (default: the current directory or its nearest parent holding ducta.yaml) |
| `--output-format` | Output format (json for scripts) — one of `rich`, `json`; default `rich` |

#### ducta ai sentinel incidents

The project's incidents, newest first

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--status` | Which incidents (default: active) — one of `active`, `open`, `remediating`, `escalated`, `resolved`, `ignored`; default `active` |
| `--env` | Only this environment's |
| `--base-path` | Project directory (default: the current directory or its nearest parent holding ducta.yaml) |
| `--output-format` | Output format (json for scripts and assistants) — one of `rich`, `json`; default `rich` |

#### ducta ai sentinel show

One incident, with its timeline

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `<incident_id>` | Incident id — *(required)* |
| `--base-path` | Project directory (default: the current directory or its nearest parent holding ducta.yaml) |
| `--output-format` | Output format (json for scripts) — one of `rich`, `json`; default `rich` |

#### ducta ai sentinel triage

What Sentinel would do about a run, without a model and without acting

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `<run_id>` | The run's certificate id — *(required)* |
| `--env` | Its environment (default: searched) |
| `--base-path` | Project directory (default: the current directory or its nearest parent holding ducta.yaml) |
| `--output-format` | Output format (json for scripts and assistants) — one of `rich`, `json`; default `rich` |

#### ducta ai sentinel watch

Run Sentinel: a pass every --interval seconds

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--env` | Environment to watch (repeatable; default: all) |
| `--interval` | Seconds between passes — default `60.0` |
| `--once` | One pass, then exit (for cron) |
| `--rerun-timeout` | Seconds one re-run may take before it is stopped (default: 4 hours) — default `14400.0` |
| `--base-path` | Project directory (default: the current directory or its nearest parent holding ducta.yaml) |
| `--output-format` | Output format (json prints each pass) — one of `rich`, `json`; default `rich` |

#### ducta ai sentinel pause

Stop Sentinel's re-runs on this project

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--reason` | Why, for the audit log — default `` |
| `--base-path` | Project directory (default: the current directory or its nearest parent holding ducta.yaml) |

#### ducta ai sentinel resume

Let Sentinel act again

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--base-path` | Project directory (default: the current directory or its nearest parent holding ducta.yaml) |

#### ducta ai sentinel resolve

Mark an incident resolved

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `<incident_id>` | Incident id — *(required)* |
| `--note` | Why, for its timeline — default `` |
| `--base-path` | Project directory (default: the current directory or its nearest parent holding ducta.yaml) |

#### ducta ai sentinel ignore

Ignore an incident

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `<incident_id>` | Incident id — *(required)* |
| `--note` | Why, for its timeline — default `` |
| `--base-path` | Project directory (default: the current directory or its nearest parent holding ducta.yaml) |

## ducta skill

Ducta ships an agent skill in the open Agent Skills format (agentskills.io): instructions, references and checks that let an AI assistant install, configure, run and debug Ducta with you. Install it where your assistant looks for skills.

### ducta skill install

Copy the skill into this project (or your home) for one or more assistants

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--target` | Assistant to install for; repeat for several. agents: Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot and others (.agents/skills); claude: Claude Code (.claude/skills); codex: Codex (.agents/skills); gemini: Gemini CLI (.gemini/skills); copilot: GitHub Copilot (.github/skills). Default: agents and claude — one of `agents`, `claude`, `codex`, `gemini`, `copilot` |
| `--global` | Install in your home directory, for every project, instead of this project |
| `--path` | Install into this skills folder instead |
| `--force` | Replace an installed skill of another version |
| `--agents` | Also install Ducta's agents (ducta-architect, ducta-sentinel) as Claude Code agent definitions in .claude/agents/ |
| `--agents-md` | Also add a short Ducta section to the project's AGENTS.md, read by assistants without skill support |

### ducta skill export

Write the skill as a zip (for claude.ai, the Skills API, others)

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--zip` | Zip file to write — default `ducta-skill.zip` |

### ducta skill path

Print where the packaged skill is
